record.paper_title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
record.original_question: Can one twist L2-invariants by finite-dimensional representations that are not necessarily unitary in a satisfactory general theory? In particular, does twisting preserve L2-Betti numbers simply by multiplying the untwisted L2-Betti number by the dimension of the representation, and for L2-torsion is the regular Fuglede-Kadison determinant continuous?

evidence.quote: A prominent open problem is whether one can twist L2-invariants with (not necessarily unitary) finite-dimensional representations.
For L2-Betti numbers there is the conjecture that this just boils down to multiplying the untwisted L2-Betti number with the dimension of the representation...
A prominent open problem is whether the regulare Fuglede-Kadison determinant is continuous, see [89, Question 9.11].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a countable discrete group and let $\mathcal{N}(G)$ denote the group von Neumann algebra of $G$, equipped with its canonical trace $\mathrm{tr}_{\mathcal{N}(G)}$. For a finitely generated Hilbert $\mathcal{N}(G)$-module $M$, let $\dim_{\mathcal{N}(G)}(M)$ denote the von Neumann dimension. For a free $G$-CW complex $X$ with finite type, the $n$-th $L^2$-Betti number is
\[ b_n^{(2)}(X;\mathcal{N}(G)) := \dim_{\mathcal{N}(G)} H_n^{(2)}(X) , \]
and when $X$ is $L^2$-acyclic and of det-class, the $L^2$-torsion $\rho^{(2)}(X)\in\mathbb{R}$ is defined via the Fuglede–Kadison determinant on $\mathcal{N}(G)$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex (not necessarily unitary) representation of $G$, viewed as a $\mathbb{C}[G]$-module of $\mathbb{C}$-dimension $d=\dim_{\mathbb{C}} V$. Twisting a $\mathbb{C}[G]$-chain complex $C_\ast$ by $V$ yields a new chain complex $C_\ast\otimes_{\mathbb{C}} V$ with a diagonal $G$-action, and one may form its associated $L^2$-completion to obtain $V$-twisted $L^2$-Betti numbers $b_n^{(2)}(X;V)$ and a $V$-twisted $L^2$-torsion $\rho^{(2)}(X;V)$.

Address the following:

(a) (Twisting conjecture for $L^2$-Betti numbers.) Prove or disprove that for every countable group $G$, every free $G$-CW complex $X$ of finite type, every $n\geq 0$, and every finite-dimensional (not necessarily unitary) complex representation $V$ of $G$,
\[ b_n^{(2)}(X;V) = (\dim_{\mathbb{C}} V)\cdot b_n^{(2)}(X;\mathcal{N}(G)). \]

(b) (Continuity of the regular Fuglede–Kadison determinant.) Decide whether the regular Fuglede–Kadison determinant $\det_{\mathcal{N}(G)}^r$ is continuous on the space of self-adjoint (or positive) operators in $\mathcal{N}(G)$ with respect to convergence in the strong operator topology together with uniform bounds on operator norms — equivalently, formulate and develop a general theory of twisted $L^2$-torsion for non-unitary finite-dimensional representations.
artifact.status_search_result: The L^2-Betti number twisting conjecture (part (a)) has been established for several classes of groups: Boschheidgen and Jaikin-Zapirain (2024) proved it for sofic groups (which include amenable and residually finite groups), and it has also been verified for locally indicable groups. The general case for arbitrary countable groups remains open, as does the continuity of the regular Fuglede–Kadison determinant (part (b)), which is a well-known open problem.

status_evidence.title: Twisted L^2-Betti numbers for sofic groups
status_evidence.snippet: The Lück twisted conjecture holds for sofic groups.
status_evidence.claim: The twisting conjecture for L^2-Betti numbers has been proven for sofic groups.

status_evidence.title: Agrarian and ℓ^2-Betti numbers of locally indicable groups, with a twist
status_evidence.snippet: twisted ℓ2-Betti numbers of locally indicable groups are equal to the usual ℓ2-Betti numbers rescaled by the dimension of the twisting representation
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture holds for locally indicable groups.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on L2-torsion (Lück)
status_evidence.snippet: open problem whether the regular Fuglede-Kadison determinant is continuous
status_evidence.claim: Continuity of the regular Fuglede–Kadison determinant remains an open problem.
